scenes.visual: Title card 'A Loop That Keeps Time' over the three stacked boxes, a small GOLD pulse ticking in the top box. COLOUR MAP, same in both films and in the lesson: GnRH GOLD; LH BLUE; FSH GREEN; testosterone and estradiol ORANGE-RED; inhibin B PURPLE; progesterone TEAL. The hypothalamus, pituitary and gonad are always three stacked rounded boxes, top to bottom, labelled 'hypothalamus', 'pituitary', 'gonad'. Cream background, 16:9. Hormone levels are schematic bars and traces labelled 'schematic'; nothing is drawn as a molecule.

scenes.tts: A man's testes keep making sperm through adult life. A woman's ovaries usually release one egg per cycle. What keeps the gonads on schedule?
scenes.visual: Left: a testis cartoon with a steady stream of tiny sperm icons leaving it, label 'through adult life'. Right: an ovary cartoon with a calendar beside it; one egg icon pops out as the calendar page flips, label 'usually one egg per cycle'. A question mark grows between them.
scenes.narration: A man's testes keep making sperm through adult life. A woman's ovaries usually release one egg per cycle. What keeps the gonads on schedule?

scenes.tts: The control sits at three levels, stacked top to bottom. The hypothalamus is at the base of the brain. The pituitary gland hangs just below it. Then come the gonads, the testes or ovaries.
scenes.visual: A brain outline slides in; the hypothalamus region lights up and lifts out as the top box. The pituitary drops in as the middle box on a short stalk. A gonad box draws at the bottom, with tiny testis and ovary icons inside, label 'gonads: testes or ovaries'.
scenes.narration: The control sits at three levels, stacked top to bottom. The hypothalamus is at the base of the brain. The pituitary gland hangs just below it. Then come the gonads, the testes or ovaries.

scenes.tts: Neurons in the hypothalamus release a hormone called G n R H, gonadotropin releasing hormone. Portal vessels carry it down to the pituitary. And it arrives in pulses, not a steady stream.
scenes.caption: Neurons in the hypothalamus release a hormone called GnRH, gonadotropin-releasing hormone. Portal vessels carry it down to the pituitary. And it arrives in pulses, not a steady stream.
scenes.visual: Inside the top box, a few neuron cartoons flash; GOLD packets, label 'GnRH', travel down a short tube labelled 'portal vessels' to the pituitary box. The packets leave in separate bursts with gaps between them, like a heartbeat. A small strip chart at the top right draws a GOLD spiky trace, label 'pulses (schematic)'. The pulses keep ticking for the rest of the film.
scenes.narration: Neurons in the hypothalamus release a hormone called GnRH, gonadotropin-releasing hormone. Portal vessels carry it down to the pituitary. And it arrives in pulses, not a steady stream.

scenes.tts: The pituitary answers with two hormones of its own, L H and F S H. They travel in the blood to the gonads. Because they act on gonads, they are called gonadotropins.
scenes.caption: The pituitary answers with two hormones of its own, LH and FSH. They travel in the blood to the gonads. Because they act on gonads, they are called gonadotropins.
scenes.visual: Each GOLD burst makes the pituitary box glow; BLUE dots ('LH') and GREEN dots ('FSH') spill into a red blood-vessel ribbon that runs down the side to the gonad box. A bracket over both colours reads 'gonadotropins'.
scenes.narration: The pituitary answers with two hormones of its own, LH and FSH. They travel in the blood to the gonads. Because they act on gonads, they are called gonadotropins.

scenes.tts: Follow them into a testis. L H reaches Leydig cells, which sit between the sperm-making tubules. They make testosterone. F S H reaches Sertoli cells, which line the tubules and support the developing sperm.
scenes.caption: Follow them into a testis. LH reaches Leydig cells, which sit between the sperm-making tubules. They make testosterone. FSH reaches Sertoli cells, which line the tubules and support the developing sperm.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the gonad box: a cross-section of three round tubules. BLUE dots land on small clusters in the gaps between tubules, label 'Leydig cells'; they glow ORANGE-RED and release ORANGE-RED dots, label 'testosterone'. GREEN dots land on tall cells lining a tubule wall, label 'Sertoli cells'; small germ cells inside the tubule step toward the centre, label 'developing sperm'.
scenes.narration: Follow them into a testis. LH reaches Leydig cells, which sit between the sperm-making tubules. They make testosterone. FSH reaches Sertoli cells, which line the tubules and support the developing sperm.

scenes.tts: Now the loop closes. Testosterone travels back up and lowers the output of the hypothalamus and the pituitary. When a product turns down its own pathway, that is negative feedback. Think of it as a brake.
scenes.visual: Zoom back out to the three boxes. ORANGE-RED dots rise up a return arrow on the right side and press on the top two boxes; a brake-pedal icon appears on the arrow, label 'negative feedback'. The BLUE and GREEN output bars beside the pituitary shrink (schematic).
scenes.narration: Now the loop closes. Testosterone travels back up and lowers the output of the hypothalamus and the pituitary. When a product turns down its own pathway, that is negative feedback. Think of it as a brake.

scenes.tts: With the brake on, L H and F S H fall. When testosterone drops, the brake eases, and L H and F S H climb back up.
scenes.caption: With the brake on, LH and FSH fall. When testosterone drops, the brake eases, and LH and FSH climb back up.
scenes.visual: A slow see-saw: the ORANGE-RED return arrow thickens and the BLUE and GREEN bars shrink; it thins and the bars grow. GOLD pulses keep ticking at the top throughout. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: With the brake on, LH and FSH fall. When testosterone drops, the brake eases, and LH and FSH climb back up.

scenes.tts: So here is a test of the loop. Remove the testes. What happens to L H and F S H in the blood? Do they go up, or down?
scenes.caption: So here is a test of the loop. Remove the testes. What happens to LH and FSH in the blood? Do they go up, or down?
scenes.visual: The gonad box fades to a dashed outline, label 'testes removed'. The BLUE and GREEN bars beside the pituitary freeze; a card reads 'LH and FSH: up or down?'
scenes.narration: So here is a test of the loop. Remove the testes. What happens to LH and FSH in the blood? Do they go up, or down?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. The question card holds; a 5-second ring timer counts down at bottom right.

scenes.tts: Both go up. With the testes gone, their testosterone is gone, so the main brake is off. The pituitary keeps driving, and L H and F S H climb.
scenes.visual: The ORANGE-RED return arrow vanishes. The BLUE and GREEN bars climb well above their earlier level, label 'LH and FSH rise (schematic)'.
scenes.caption: Both go up. With the testes gone, their testosterone is gone, so the main brake is off. The pituitary keeps driving, and LH and FSH climb.
scenes.narration: Both go up. With the testes gone, their testosterone is gone, so the main brake is off. The pituitary keeps driving, and LH and FSH climb.

scenes.tts: F S H has a second brake of its own. Sertoli cells release a hormone called inhibin B, which lowers F S H. Remove the testes, and that brake goes too.
scenes.caption: FSH has a second brake of its own. Sertoli cells release a hormone called inhibin B, which lowers FSH. Remove the testes, and that brake goes too.
scenes.visual: Rewind to the intact loop: a second, PURPLE return arrow labelled 'inhibin B' rises from the Sertoli cells and presses only on the GREEN FSH bar. Then the gonad box dashes out again and the PURPLE arrow fades with the ORANGE-RED one.
scenes.narration: FSH has a second brake of its own. Sertoli cells release a hormone called inhibin B, which lowers FSH. Remove the testes, and that brake goes too.

scenes.tts: The ovary runs on the same loop. There the brake comes from the follicle, the sac of cells around a growing egg. Its hormone, estradiol, brakes the loop through most of the cycle's first half. But when estradiol stays high for long enough, the brake becomes an accelerator. After ovulation, progesterone brakes instead. The lesson shows how.
scenes.visual: The gonad box now holds an ovary with one growing follicle, label 'follicle: egg plus supporting cells', that releases ORANGE-RED dots, label 'estradiol'. The ORANGE-RED return arrow presses on the top boxes with the brake icon; a calendar strip runs along the bottom, its first half labelled 'follicular phase'. Late in that half, as the ORANGE-RED level holds high, the brake icon turns into an accelerator-pedal icon, label 'high for long enough: accelerator'. After a small 'ovulation' tick, a TEAL arrow labelled 'progesterone' takes over the brake icon for the second half. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: The ovary runs on the same loop. There the brake comes from the follicle, the sac of cells around a growing egg. Its hormone, estradiol, brakes the loop through most of the cycle's first half. But when estradiol stays high for long enough, the brake becomes an accelerator. After ovulation, progesterone brakes instead. The lesson shows how.

scenes.tts: One thing is still odd. G n R H reaches the pituitary in bursts, not a stream. Is the burst just how it travels, or is it the message?
scenes.caption: One thing is still odd. GnRH reaches the pituitary in bursts, not a stream. Is the burst just how it travels, or is it the message?
scenes.visual: Zoom to the GOLD burst train in the portal tube. A thought bubble shows the same GOLD amount as one smooth stream beside the bursts, with a question mark between them.
scenes.narration: One thing is still odd. GnRH reaches the pituitary in bursts, not a stream. Is the burst just how it travels, or is it the message?

scenes.tts: So the brain drives the gonads in pulses, through the pituitary. And the gonads' hormones come back up as a brake, almost all the time.
scenes.visual: Recap: the full three-box loop. GOLD pulses down, BLUE and GREEN down to the gonad, ORANGE-RED and PURPLE arrows back up with brake icons. Small tag on the ovary side: 'ovulatory cycle: estradiol held high -> LH surge'.
scenes.narration: So the brain drives the gonads in pulses, through the pituitary. And the gonads' hormones come back up as a brake, almost all the time.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex. LINE: 'The brain drives the gonads in pulses; gonad hormones brake the brain.'
